bibliographic.title: Machine Learning based Enterprise Financial Audit Framework and High Risk Identification
bibliographic.authors: Tingyu Yuan, Xi Zhang, Xuanjing Chen
bibliographic.citation_apa: Yuan, T., Zhang, X., & Chen, X. (unclear). Machine Learning based Enterprise Financial Audit Framework and High Risk Identification. unclear.

methodology.study_design: comparative algorithm benchmarking with hierarchical K-fold cross-validation and classification metrics (F1-score, accuracy, recall)
methodology.sample_description: Dataset from the Big Four accounting firms (EY, PwC, Deloitte, KPMG) spanning 2020 to 2025, including audit project counts, high-risk cases, detected frauds, compliance breaches, employee workload, client satisfaction, and AI auxiliary role indicators
methodology.technology_context: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) for high-risk identification, fraud detection, and compliance anomaly detection in enterprise financial audit

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Study addresses classical machine learning for enterprise financial audit risk prediction; provided text contains no large language models, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper covers regulated financial auditing, compliance, risk assessment, and corporate governance themes, it operationalizes governance through ML-based audit automation and risk prediction rather than conversational AI governance. The review scope requires LLM-based conversational systems and associated governance; this mismatch is explicit in the abstract and introduction.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is clear from provided text: only SVM, RF, and KNN are discussed; no conversational or LLM governance content appears.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on abstract and partial full text only. Study appears methodologically coherent for ML audit risk classification, but dataset size, provenance validation, and ethics are not detailed in the excerpt provided.

cerqual.explanation: Internal coherence of the ML audit framework is reasonably described, but relevance to conversational governance in LLM systems is very low based on the supplied text.

coding.theme: Machine learning for enterprise financial audit and high-risk identification
coding.subtheme: Comparative evaluation of SVM, Random Forest, and KNN on Big Four audit data

synthesis.main_claim: Random Forest outperforms SVM and KNN for enterprise financial audit high-risk identification, achieving an F1-score of 0.9012, especially in fraud and compliance anomaly detection.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an AI-driven financial audit framework using classical machine learning to improve audit efficiency, accuracy, and risk management in regulated enterprise environments.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpt does not fully report study limitations, dataset size, or external validity constraints; future work mentions deep learning integration but details are incomplete in supplied text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central evidence on conversational governance in LLM systems; at most peripheral contextual background for regulated financial audit automation using pre-LLM machine learning.
